content.title: About
content.content: Tomato and cucumber salad is made from fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, vegetable oil and vinegar. It is a light, refreshing dish popular in summer, low in calories and easy to prepare.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health.
Cucumbers are composed of more than 95% water, making them an excellent source of hydration.
The combination of vinegar and oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables.
In Russian cuisine the classic “Olivier” salad often includes tomatoes, but here they are the star ingredient.
The salad can be served as a standalone dish or as a side to meat and fish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Both tomatoes and cucumbers provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: High water content and low fat make this salad suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes healthy bowel function and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene and other phytochemicals in tomatoes protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Cucumbers help maintain the body’s fluid balance due to their high water content.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: A large amount of vinegar can increase stomach acidity and cause discomfort for people with gastritis.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If the vegetables are not organic, they may contain pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, tossing the sliced vegetables with a mixture of oil and vinegar. Add fresh herbs, spices, or a pinch of salt to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, keep the dressing separate to prevent the vegetables from becoming soggy.
